title: Tiny SDKs: Air-gap onboarding checklist + 30min hacklab notes (experimental)
text:
Tiny SDKs: Air-gap onboarding checklist + 30min hacklab notes (experimental)

summary:
Working notes for a minimal, air-gapped SDK distribution and a 30-minute internal hacklab to validate onboarding flows. Focus is on ultra-small footprint (<=50MB), deterministic deps, offline docs, signed artifacts, and simple KMS/HSM integration patterns for token provisioning.

objectives:
Define a repeatable checklist to produce an air-gapped SDK artifact users can install without network access
Create a 30-minute lab flow that a new engineer can follow to get a sample app calling the Redwood Private endpoint (mocked) using offline credentials
Identify minimal telemetry/observability that respects air-gap constraints
Surface security and licensing decisions (signing, checksums, trust chain)

constraints:
No outbound network from target environment during install
Total downloaded artifact for SDK + native deps <= 50MB (goal)
Only allow signed/verified artifacts by default
Must support KMS/HSM token injection workflow used by enterprise customers

prereqs:
Host: Linux x86_64 (container-friendly) or Windows x64 (optional)
A machine used to create offline bundle with internet access (build host)
Customer org provides public key/certificate for signature verification or we publish our public signing key via secure channel
A mock Redwood Private endpoint (local docker image) for hacklab or an on-prem sandbox with allowed IPs

distribution_options:
Signed tarball (.tar.gz) containing a single static binary + LICENSE + offline README
OCI image exported as tar (docker save) with layers pinned and SHA verified
Signed ZIP with an included installer script that verifies binary signature before install
Native OS packages (deb/rpm) for customers who require package manager installs (stretch goal)

onboard_checklist:
Build static binary with MUSL or static linking to avoid runtime dependency surprises
Strip debug symbols and compress with upx (optional) to meet size goal
Produce deterministic builds: record build environment, Go/Rust/Python versions, and exact dependency SHAs
Sign artifact using CI signing key and publish checksum file alongside the bundle
Create offline README with step-by-step install and a minimal quickstart example
Add an offline credential injection example using PKCS#11/HSM or a local file-based token with instructions to rotate
Include a verification script that checks signature + checksum before executing
Package a small smoke-test harness that runs locally and verifies token usage and endpoint reachability (mocked)

30min-hacklab-flow:
0-05m: Intro + goals (facilitator explains constraints and expected outcome)
05-10m: Copy pre-built bundle to lab VM (artifact already on USB or internal file share)
10-18m: Run verification script (signature + checksum) and install binary to ~/bin
18-25m: Inject test credentials: option A - local PKCS#11 mock; option B - file-based token placed in ./creds
25-28m: Run sample app to call mocked Redwood Private endpoint (local docker) and confirm expected response
28-30m: Quick debrief: failures/observability + capture one action item per group

smoke_tests:
Binary exits 0 on --version and prints build metadata (commit SHA, built-at)
Verification script rejects tampered artifact (checksum/signature mismatch)
Sample app authenticates with provided token and receives 200 from mock endpoint
Sample app fails with clear error code when token missing or invalid
Offline README opens and includes at least one reproducible troubleshooting step

observability_and_telemetry_plan:
No outbound telemetry by default — opt-in via explicit env var and offline upload instructions
Provide a local JSON diagnostics dump command that writes logs, config, and last request traces to disk for collection
Include a small collector script that can package diagnostics for secure transfer to support
Telemetry payloads must be human-reviewable and compressible (gzip) for constrained transfer processes

rollback_and_failure_modes:
If verification fails, installer aborts and recommends contacting security + provides offline troubleshooting steps
If KMS/HSM integration fails, fall back to a local secure token file with clear expiration and rotation guidance
If binary crashes on first run, support harness runs --diag and packages logs for upload
Network calls to Redwood Private should have a strict timeout and a local offline mode that returns deterministic canned responses for UX testing

open_questions:
Which CI-managed signing key will be used for production SDK artifacts? (security to decide)
Do we provide official PKCS#11 helpers or expect customers to wire their own HSMs?
Acceptable max artifact size: 50MB is aspirational — should we allow larger images for Windows?
Should we maintain a separate "airgap" branch of SDKs or a single artifact with feature flags?

next_steps:
(Arjun) Prototype static binary build pipeline and report compressed artifact size by 2025-03-10
(Lena) Draft signing + verification spec for review by Security (PR to confluence) by 2025-03-07
(Diego) Prepare mock dockerized Redwood Private sandbox for the hacklab and publish instructions
(Sophie) Organize a 30-minute pilot run with Solutions Engineers and capture notes

notes:
This doc is intentionally light on implementation detail — it's a working checklist to drive a short internal experiment. Keep ephemeral links in linked_artifacts; move finalized specs to Confluence once decisions made.
